2607.21570.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
2607.21570.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise for medical education, but most existing systems focus on localized interactions such as question answering or single-turn feedback, rather than organizing an entire clinical case into a decision-centered learning trajectory. We introduce \textit{MedGame}, a framework that transforms static clinical cases into structured, executable storytelling games. MedGame uses a dual-engine design: a Medical Narrative Designer synthesizes case-grounded clinical storylines with states and decision nodes, while a Story Director converts them into dependency-aware multimodal orchestration plans rendered by our released interactive platform. We construct MedGame Bench, a 5,000-case benchmark and evaluation protocol for Medical Narrative Generation and Story Direction. Experiments show that task-specific fine-tuning substantially improves open-source LLMs on MedGame Bench and narrows the gap with commercial models. A pilot student study further shows that learners perceive MedGame as more engaging and useful than text-only alternatives.
2607.21570.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在醫學教育中顯示出潛力，但大多數現有系統專注於局部互動，例如問題回答或單回合反饋，而不是將整個臨床案例組織成以決策為中心的學習軌跡。<lb/>我們介紹了\textit{MedGame}，一個將靜態臨床案例轉化為結構化、可執行的敘事遊戲的框架。<lb/>MedGame採用雙引擎設計：醫學敘事設計師將基於案例的臨床故事情節與狀態和決策節點綜合，而故事導演則將其轉換為依賴感知的多模態協調計劃，這些計劃由我們發布的互動平台呈現。<lb/>我們構建了MedGame Bench，一個包含5,000個案例的基準和醫學敘事生成及故事導向的評估協議。<lb/>實驗顯示，針對特定任務的微調顯著提高了開源LLMs在MedGame Bench上的表現，並縮小了與商業模型之間的差距。<lb/>一項初步的學生研究進一步顯示，學習者認為MedGame比僅有文本的替代方案更具吸引力和實用性。
